text:
lin: quick RFC follow-up — we need a pragmatic plan for rate-tier fallback decisions when telemetry is delayed. current runtime uses last-seen latency/cost signals with a 60s ttl. proposal: emit a lightweight policy-epoch id + telemetry-watermark so runtimes can decide when to fully apply new penalty weights. thoughts?

arjun: short question — what's the exact failure mode we're avoiding? oscillation during region failovers?

lin: yep. observed a few incidents where region probe spikes flip penalties, hedging reacts, traffic shifts, then probes look worse and it flips back -> cascade. goal is avoid flip-flop while still being reasonably reactive.

maria: +1 to explicit epoch ids. can we reuse route-config checksum or should this be separate?

keith: prefer separate. checksum conflates unrelated proto changes. epoch + per-region watermark (monotonic) signals readiness.

arjun: tradeoff: delaying weight application reduces reactivity. what target reactivity do we want? 5s / 30s / 60s?

lin: thinking two-tier approach: 1) soft-apply new weights immediately with a dampening factor (e.g. scale 0.5) so runtime can probe but not preempt; 2) hard-swap to full weights after either watermark seen for region OR after 20s fallback. this balances stability and reactivity.

keith: how would this look in policy proto? sketch:

```
policy_epoch: "2026-03-22T12:34:56Z"
soft_apply: true
soft_scale: 0.5
telemetry_watermark: [ { region: "us-west-2", seq: 12345 }, { region: "eu-west-1", seq: 9876 } ]
hard_swap_timeout_secs: 20
```

maria: for telemetry size concerns: runtimes only need a small watermark / seq number. full histograms are optional and can be sampled. runtime can call /telemetry/summary to confirm counts. keep heartbeat tiny.

arjun: control-plane chatter is a concern if every runtime polls. can we push instead of poll? or use long-poll with backoff?

lin: push is nicer but more complex across private deployments. suggest long-poll + exponential backoff + jitter. also runtime config flag to opt-in: policy_consistency=best_effort. default on for hosted/dedicated. opt-out for air-gapped private.

keith: add randomized stagger for hard_swap_timeout to avoid synchronized swaps (jitter 0..3s).

maria: also add probe tagging: telemetry samples should include tag probe=true so policy ignores synthetic load spikes. small change to our probe infra.

ops-bot: :information_source: policy-rollout-bot: started rollout epoch 2026-03-22T12:34:56Z -> 3 clusters (usw2, eu1, ap1)

arjun: tests? we should run sim-harness with: (a) delayed telemetry by 10-30s, (b) region probe spike, (c) mix of probe/real traffic. measure oscillation count and cost.

lin: agreed. i'll add sim scenarios and target metrics: reduce flip count by >70% and keep median failover latency < 8s.

keith: one more: metrics/alerts — when runtimes fallback to hard_swap_timeout due to missing watermark we should emit a metric policy.hard_swap.fallback{region,epoch}.ops can track weird control-plane lag.

maria: ack. i'll add telemetry tags and sampling plan in the RFC PR.

lin: great. i'll draft the RFC update and a policy-proto PR with fields above + docs for runtime behavior. will include a small sample sim and perf targets. @arjun @keith please review when I post. :thumbsup:

keith: :thumbsup:

arjun: looks reasonable, thanks lin.

maria: thanks!
